reviews.text: "Chloe Domont’s Fair Play is a slick psychological thriller that takes unwavering aim at ambition, jealousy, and the corrosive nature of secrecy."
reviews.author: Jack Walters

reviews.text: Turning this power-driven human drama into a sweaty palm, pulse-pounding thriller may be one of the most subversive moves we’ve seen a filmmaker make recently.
reviews.author: James Preston Poole

reviews.text: In her unpredictable feature debut, writer-director Chloe Domont stares down toxic relationships and deconstructs the dynamic with masterful exposition.
reviews.author: Brittany Patrice Witherspoon

reviews.text: Reminiscent of the hit television drama Industry, director Chloe Domont’s debut feature on two ambitious financial analysts caught in a doomed relationship is slick, sexy and all kinds of enjoyable.
reviews.author: Gautam Sunder

reviews.text: And old-school suspense thriller...You won't believe the ending. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Rivera Rubio

reviews.text: Effective sound design and solid acting anchor an overdetermined and melodramatic plot.
reviews.author: CJ Sheu

reviews.text: In his debut feature, Dumont demonstrates a great narrative pulse, crafting a thriller that works like a pressure cooker, with a payoff that is as inevitable as it is surprising.
reviews.author: Valentina Morillo

reviews.text: The plot of Netflix's 'Fair Play', is a brilliant combination between erotic thriller, contemporary ambition and violence. All in the middle of the most sophisticated financial scenario. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Aglaia Berlutti

reviews.text: What should become a raging fire of betrayal and deceit never generates more candlepower than a plug-in air freshener.
reviews.author: Mike Scott

reviews.text: A seductive thriller that meticulously explores corporate greed and gender politics.
reviews.author: Jordy Sirkin

reviews.text: A great surprise...It has the feel of a lost erotic thriller from the 80s or 90s, and yet, the story is given modern sensibilities.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: Fair Play is a thorny, gnarly, tangled web that’s woven by Domont’s deft hands.
reviews.author: Tina Kakadelis

reviews.text: Fair Play features two phenomenal and emotional performances at the center, and there is an intensity that will have viewers locked in until the end.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: Domont creates a story to not only expose how deep-seated patriarchal norms are in corporate culture, but to also honestly portray how its victims will often attempt to believe those hurting them most are still worth saving.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: An off-putting exercise in workplace intrigue, full of slick surfaces, performative smoking, and people horndogging in suspiciously forceful ways.
reviews.author: Robert Horton

reviews.text: Avoiding the restrictions of a standard erotic thriller, this brutal drama expertly and equally explores the explosive passions of its two characters in a truthful, vivid, and unflinching way.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: First-time feature director Chloe Domont knows how to draw the audience in. The way she builds tension with the most minimal devices, utilizing the already-strained dynamics of a hedge fund company and a rich arsenal of quips, is immensely pleasurable.
reviews.author: Savina Petkova

reviews.text: A provocative thriller that explores the gender dynamics in today's world. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: ...a solid drama that benefits substantially from the top-tier efforts of its stars...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: Regardless of how you feel about stock market films, this exceptionally well-acted relationship thriller is guaranteed to entertain, even if it will ruin Alden Ehrenreich for you (because he's so hissably awful)
reviews.author: Joe Lipsett

reviews.text: The dedicated performances from Phoebe Dyvenor and Alden Ehrenreich make it a gripping viewing experience, emphasizing the film's thought-provoking messages about gender politics and seeking equal recognition based on merit rather than gender.
reviews.author: Manuel São Bento

reviews.text: Writer-director Chloe Domont engulfs us in a world of awfulness, and leaves us, and her characters, there to wallow in it. ... It’s like trying to care about the result of a game in a sport for which you have zero interest.
reviews.author: Tim Miller

reviews.text: Wants to take a giant leap forward to get to its chief beef but that swiftness strains credulity with co-workers oblivious to the central relationship until taking another hard turn into what is possibly supposed to be satirical carnage that doesn't land.
reviews.author: Erik Childress

reviews.text: It touches a nerve with topics such as abusive corporation treatment and sexual harassment. However, it falls short of realizing its full potential, with a conclusion that doesn't quite measure up to the rest of the narrative.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: Excels at tugging one strand of a rug and yanking the entire thing out from under two people who thought they could handle anything.
reviews.author: Matt Pais

reviews.text: The risk in the screenplay involves getting ahead at the office. All of the film’s acting is superb. The extraordinary performances from Dynevor and Ehrenreich are electrifying. If Academy Award voters are brave, acting nominations are deserved.
reviews.author: Michael Calleri

reviews.text: This is one of those movies where the thematics undermine the characters, where everyone just seem to be a piece on the chessboard.
reviews.author: Wade Major

reviews.text: Initially it works, and then it devolves into something so extreme that it becomes borderline silly.
reviews.author: Claudia Puig

reviews.text: After carefully steering it to within touching distance of David Fincher’s Gone Girl — the pinnacle of this sort of cinema, at least in the last decade  — Domont appears to have a change of heart as she swerves towards a ‘safer’, more conventional ending.
reviews.author: Rohan Naahar

reviews.text: While Chloe Domont’s debut feature overcooks things in its final throes, it leaves us with some meat to chew on.
reviews.author: Hilary A White

reviews.text: Watching Fair Play sometimes feels like observing a slow-motion traffic accident, but it gets at enduring conflicts between men and women in ways that few movies have.
reviews.author: Margot Harrison

reviews.text: ... Perversion, desire, and pleasure come together like an explosive combo, which the director handles deftly. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: A film with a distinctive personality and an eagerness to dig around in the real-world sandbox and ask questions for which it knows there is no single, pat set of answers. Fair Play never stops making moves, which makes even its missteps feel refreshing.
reviews.author: Brent Simon

reviews.text: Anchored by strong work from Phoebe Dynevor and Alden Ehrenreich it is hard not to be drawn into Fair Play -- even as the film becomes more and more uncomfortable to watch.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: A riveting exposition on sexism, ego and gender wrapped up in a taught and intelligent office thriller.
reviews.author: Dustin Chase

reviews.text: It's one of the more incisive and powerfully made movies about relationship dynamics in a good long while.
reviews.author: Robert Levin

reviews.text: Straining for credulity in the tough, fast-moving world of financial services, the film's appealing young romantic couple each have a point to make in the power-play, in this good-looking but oddly even-handed thriller
reviews.author: Jane Freebury

reviews.text: Fair Play has a lot to say, and the semi-autobiographical nature of the script (by director, Chloe Dumont) is evident with plenty of post-screening discussion points. Unfortunately, it falls flat in the third act.
reviews.author: Bren Murphy

reviews.text: It isn’t that it goes in a different direction from what we’d hoped that gives us hesitation in recommending it, however, but, instead, it’s its over-the-top final act that doesn’t track with what comes before it.
reviews.author: Mark Meszoros

reviews.text: A steamy tale of smoldering jealousy in the brutal world of high finance...brought to white-hot life by bravura performances by Dynevor and Ehrenreich, and a coolly calculated turn by Marsan.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: What Fair Play can’t quite deliver is the nuance needed to make these comparisons between men and women unique or new, and to push itself past archetypes and parables.
reviews.author: Roxana Hadadi

reviews.text: Perversely provocative and shamelessly entertaining.
reviews.author: Eleanor Ringel Cater

reviews.text: A compelling, astute and brilliantly acted tale of how modern relationships can still be warped and wiped away by traditions in the workplace.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: Phoebe Dynevor and Alden Ehrenreich star in Chloe Domont's debut feature, a brilliant dissection of fragile masculinity with a promotion as a trigger. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Janire Zurbano

reviews.text: Oddly, as the story's tension rises, the film becomes less involving, abandoning wit and authenticity for arch melodrama.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: Fair Play is combative, unpleasant, and absolutely brilliant.
reviews.author: Natasha Alvar

reviews.text: A powerhouse movie that should go to the top of your Netflix watch list.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: There is certainly a lot to love in Fair Play, from Dynevor and Ehrenreich's chemistry to white-knuckle scenes of hedge fund intrigue. But the film can't fulfill its own ambitious attempts to interrogate the intersections of power, gender, and ego.
reviews.author: Belen Edwards

reviews.text: Great work from the two protagonists, an achieved atmosphere of tension, and good management of how everything deteriorates lead to the perfect ending. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mikel Zorrilla

reviews.text: Fair Play is, essentially, an intense drama that some previous opinions classified as an erotic thriller, although it is legitimately decaffeinated in this subject... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rafael Santisteban

reviews.text: Fair Play is the immersive and compelling story of a seemingly-unbreakable-partnership-turned-toxic that you won’t easily forget.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: A sizzling directorial debut from Chloe Domont with career defining performances from Phoebe Dynevor and Alden Ehrenrich.
reviews.author: Lauren Veneziani

reviews.text: Luke might not mind a bit of period sex, but seeing his fiancé as his professional superior? Now that’s a boner-killer.
reviews.author: Katie Parker

reviews.text: Both [Phoebe] Dynevor and [Alden] Ehrenreich share great chemistry and their love-hate relationship is part of the reasons that made Fair Play such a thought-provoking experience.
reviews.author: Casey Chong

reviews.text: Destined to court controversy, screenwriter/director Chloe Domont's adult -entangling, insightful view of gender dynamics is a compelling psychological thriller for the post-#MeToo era, as she imbues the ensuing histrionics with a veil of validity.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: The characters created by Dynevor and Ehrenreich are bland and boring.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: It’s hard to combine sex, danger, and stars with erotic chemistry. But just when you wonder if anyone can reach the zenith of the 80s and 90s and create a new BODY HEAT or BASIC INSTINCT, along comes FAIR PLAY and it truly thrills.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: Fair Play transcends its shortcomings and becomes one of the most thrilling directorial debuts this year.
reviews.author: Siddhant Adlakha

reviews.text: Fair Play uses elements of thrillers and melodrama that function like a pot that is heated to its boiling point. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Emiliano Basile

reviews.text: Fair Play is a far cry from 9 to 5; it fearlessly updates the male-female workplace power dynamic to modern standards, which is to say, it paints a portrait of male toxicity that pushes past amorality to near-fatality. And it’s riveting.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: While the story arc is obvious and predictable, the tone of the narrative is complemented nicely by the cinematography and lighting, maintaining the turbulent agitation as emotions flare.
reviews.author: Chris Joyce

reviews.text: It's a "relationship thriller" because you don't know exactly where it's gonna go, the tension is always there, and you can see it in how they [the main characters] look at each other..and there is so much under the surface.
reviews.author: Michael Cook

reviews.text: In a high-stakes environment, the egos on display are heightened here, setting up shifting dynamics, and sinister overtones. That explosive tension forces this off the rails in the third act, going from uncomfortable to painful as it strains credibility.
reviews.author: Lynn Venhaus

reviews.text: Fair Play is a spectacular drama, a painful crash of broken love and a sharp look at the fragility of the male ego in the business world.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: Fair Play is a film with tonal shifts that aren’t always executed well. That said, once it finds its footing it’s a stark and uncomfortable look at a deteriorating relationship that races toward an unhinged uncertainty that pays tension off.
reviews.author: Kate Sánchez

reviews.text: An uncomfortable yet engrossing watch, this is an astonishingly tight debut from Domont.
reviews.author: Sarah Cook

reviews.text: An impressive feature debut from Chloe Domont, her shrewd script & assured direction make for a tense + twisted corporate thriller that makes your skin crawl.
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: With star-making performances by Alden Ehrenreich and Phoebe Dynevor, this movie is not messing around, which makes it one of the best Netflix releases of the year.
reviews.author: Mireia Mullor

reviews.text: https://kkfi.org/program-episodes/freeze-frame-the-exorcist-believer-r-fair-play-r-the-royal-hotel-r-totally-killer-r/
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: Benefitting from intimate cinematography and committed performances, the film paints gutsy and psychologically plausible portraits of a toxic workplace and an increasingly twisted relationship.
reviews.author: Emma Simmonds

reviews.text: Domont carefully crafts a cautionary tale of male fragility with powerhouse performances by Phoebe Dynevor and Alden Ehrenreich which propel the erotic thriller into the stratosphere. As gender roles are redefined, Domont takes us to a shocking climax.
reviews.author: Joe Friar

reviews.text: Not even the habitual and confusing banking language can calm down this intelligent erotic thriller about gender politics and high finance Darwinism.  [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: Like the riskiest stocks on the market, Fair Play dips and rallies in patterns I could never truly pin down. Just when it appears to be trending upward, it plummets even lower.
reviews.author: Layla McMurtrie

reviews.text: It’s ultimately a very ugly film. That’s not its failure, but its intention.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: hough the film constantly seems poised to deliver something insightful, it never finds any depth, thus leaving the viewer with frustratingly little to care about. In the end, it just feels like one long tease.
reviews.author: Shirley Li

reviews.text: At its best, Fair Play feels like a demented game where everything in high finance comes down to how you project yourself, man or woman.
reviews.author: Jake Coyle

reviews.text: As verbal wounds escalate into literal bruises, we realize Domont has tricked us to invest our own empathy in these two emotionally bankrupt young lovers who can accept volatility in the stock market — but not in themselves.
reviews.author: Amy Nicholson

reviews.text: While well shot and cleverly conceived in its early goings by writer/director Chloe Domont, I feel like Fair Play spins its wheels moreso than just ramps up the tension.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: Not only must credit be given for how well-written the characters are and the crispness of the dialogue, but also the work of the two leads.  Ehrenreich is one of our most underrated screen actors, while Dynevor is a revelation.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: Fair Play is an effective, if slightly overlong, acidic relationship drama, a kind of Who’s Afraid of Virginia Woolf? set among the world of high finance and insecure men.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: Great productions elements to it with the score, cinematography, great directorial debut and strong performances especially from Phoebe but the lack of relationship building to get to where they end up should’ve been more of the focus to start.
reviews.author: Elliott Collins

reviews.text: While it didn’t work for me, ultimately, I do hope it does well so that people might be allowed to make good thrillers again.
reviews.author: Julian Lytle

reviews.text: A bum ending doesn’t deflate the endeavor, which examines psychological poisoning brilliantly, working right to the core of humiliation.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: Tense, at times perverse, but above all intelligent and bold, this first feature film by Chloe Domont positions her as a filmmaker to follow closely... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: The two characters are so unlikable you just don’t care how any of it turns out.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: It’s a sharp, cruel movie that’s hard to “recommend” in some respects, but it sure does leave a lacerating impression.
reviews.author: Dennis Harvey

reviews.text: Fair Play shows a clear willingness to portray the sexual desire of its lead characters as well as how their career paths can set them at war with each other. As the film continues, it asks some deep and dark questions.
reviews.author: Eamon Hennedy

reviews.text: With sly effectiveness in hanging on every stare between the words, that’s how a movie like "Fair Play" gets you.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: This workplace psycho-romance traces the resentments that can asphyxiate a couple when one partner’s career escalates as the other’s falters, and it does so in the service of a bigger picture.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: Sizzling, relevant, and smart filmmaking which acts as a hell of a cinematic calling card for Domont.
reviews.author: Nadine Whitney

reviews.text: Fair Play is for the most part a smart, modern update to those wince-inducing erotic office thrillers from the Nineties starring Demi Moore, Michael Douglas and a floppy disc.
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: The cast is riveting and the insights into the poisonous priorities of people who know the cost of everything and the value of nothing at all paint a picture of modern corporate treachery.
reviews.author: Rex Reed

reviews.text: One of the shrewdest takes on the erotic thriller in recent memory.
reviews.author: Natalia Winkelman

reviews.text: Fair Play is a tantalising, seductive drama that never aims to be blatantly feminist, but a film with a more broad appeal – and that is a compliment.
reviews.author: Maria Lattila

reviews.text: It’s maliciously effective, up to a point: an enjoyably lurid piece of classy-trashy psychological warfare.
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

reviews.text: “Fair Play” is the edgiest, coolest, sexiest and most provocative film of the year!  Don't miss it!
reviews.author: Leah Sydney

reviews.text: For those still experiencing "Succession" withdrawal or who are anxiously awaiting the third season of HBO's "Industry," "Fair Play" is a more than satisfactory fix.
reviews.author: Cary Darling

reviews.text: A tough Dynevor from Netflix's "Bridgerton, and the credible Ehrenreich, following his underrated supporting turn in "Oppenheimer," strut their surprising stuff like seasoned old pros.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: Fair Play is a hauntingly realistic depiction of toxic masculinity and sexual politics centered within the cutthroat and challenging world of high finance. Phoebe Dynevor and Alden Ehrenreich expertly portray their complex, dynamic characters.
reviews.author: Amanda Mazzillo

reviews.text: A searing, nicely sordid psychosexual thriller in the world of high finance...
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: Fair Play is a smart, twisty mix of romance and corporate politics.
reviews.author: Dann Gire

reviews.text: Sometimes you are not prepared for what a film has to deliver. This is exactly the feeling with this erotic thriller that gives you a firm slap around the face in the first scene to get you enthralled.
reviews.author: Dulcie Pearce

reviews.text: It begins with the blood of a woman and ends with the blood of a man. But it’s what transpires between that proves most captivating in Chloe Domont’s auspicious filmmaking debut.
reviews.author: Al Alexander

reviews.text: Fair Play may represent a worst-case scenario for its unfortunate couple, but its searing observations about fragility and the male ego don’t feel too far off from reality.
reviews.author: Tanner Gordon

reviews.text: Domont resists turning her film into a series of juicy and meaningless sex scenes, preferring to use them as a smart, psychologically complex status bar for the central couple.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: Fair Play really does manage to play fair in terms of balancing our antipathy with our voyeuristic interest in what’s happening.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: The film has a propulsion to it that keeps it interesting, and the intensity of the final sequence is sufficient to forgive any earlier missteps.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: When a hedge fund promotes a she (Phoebe Dynevor) over a he (Alden Ehrenreich)—they’re engaged— gender politics becomes a powerhouse erotic thriller which newbie filmmaker Chloe Domont wants couples to leave arguing like hell. No worries. They  will.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: It’s a smart, simmering, absolutely gripping little thriller, and it deserves every bit of hype and attention that’s about to come its way.
reviews.author: Matthew Jackson

reviews.text: By teasing weighty gender power questions and resolving them so unpleasantly, writer/director Chloe Domont’s film will either be widely embraced or harshly reviled. I’m somewhere in between.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: Fair Play is a cage match...Chloe Domont never picks sides but instead leaves you to pick your poison. Because the poison is the point.
reviews.author: Sherin Nicole

reviews.text: Would you like a side of erotic revenge this evening? How about a nightcap of noir? If you have a taste for the savage, you might easily split the difference with “Fair Play.”
reviews.author: Susie Bright

reviews.text: While the sensational elements stop it short of thoughtful discourse, Fair Play takes the best elements of the adult thriller and makes them relevant to today.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: Fair Play keeps us involved, even during the times when we wonder whether Domont might be pushing things too far.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: [A] thriller, which stars Phoebe Dynevor and Alden Ehrenreich, two beautiful people who embody the genre with a seamless ease, evokes those late-‘80s and early-‘90s flicks in a way that’s assuredly entertaining.
reviews.author: Emily Zemler

reviews.text: Chloe Domont beats a sly, perceptive path across this tricky psychological turf.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: An office romance is put to the test in a tense and dynamic drama.
reviews.author: Karen Gordon

reviews.text: As cultural critique, Fair Play plays along with our queasy, admiring engagement with great wealth. The focus remains on the way business poisons the lives of two people -- rather than attempting to underline the flaws of capitalism.
reviews.author: Steve Erickson

reviews.text: It’s moody and tense, and it features captivating performances from its leads, Alden Ehrenreich and Phoebe Dynevor. But it’s peppered with false moments that undercut the experience, repeatedly pulling the viewer out of the action.
reviews.author: Esther Zuckerman

reviews.text: Everything about this story feels like a fait accompli.
reviews.author: Matt Singer

reviews.text: Written and directed by Chloe Domont, and inspired by her own experiences as an up-and-coming filmmaker, Fair Play works well as a relationship drama, an erotic thriller, and as high finance intrigue. It’s also tremendously insightful.
reviews.author: Jorge Ignacio Castillo

reviews.text: Present-day erotic thriller well-versed in matters of gender and the dynamics of corporate byplay, akin to the genre’s intelligent entries of the 1980s and 1990s—Domont’s no Paul Verhoeven, but who is?
reviews.author: Ray Pride

reviews.text: A gripping first feature from an impressive new talent that will get people talking both at work and at home.
reviews.author: Neil Smith

reviews.text: Domont’s premise is a provocative one, and she crafts expertly cutting dialogue around it.
reviews.author: Kimberley Jones

reviews.text: Nothing about Fair Play is subtle. Rather, it is slick, sexy, and, at times, delightfully shocking.
reviews.author: Sarah Gorr

reviews.text: If there are ragged edges to Domont’s first feature, the film is also impressively serrated.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: Beginning with a tantalizing premise ... Fair Play quickly spirals out of control.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: The film is neither a stern lecture nor cheap entertainment, with Domont instead threading the needle somewhere in-between to create a tense guessing game of just how far she will push her characters.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: A tense, engrossing psychological thriller about power dynamics, gender roles and workplace relationships, powered by great performances by Phoebe Dynevor and Alden Ehrenreich. An impressive directing debut by Chloe Domont. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: Acting is not the strong suit here. The characters are two-dimensional, at best, with no notable performances. Even the always reliable Eddie Marsen, as the ruthless head corporate honcho, seems to phone in his performance.
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: Luke becomes such a flat character that his unhinged behavior turns into white noise.
reviews.author: David Bax

reviews.text: You're not ready for Fair Play, an erotic thriller wrapped in barbed wire that throws back to the genre's '80s and '90s heyday while rooting itself firmly in the present.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: This taut erotic thriller stars Phoebe Dynevor and Alden Ehrenreich as a couple whose relationship is poisoned when one is promoted at their cutthroat investment firm.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: The sex scenes between leads Phoebe Dynevor and Alden Ehrenreich do a great job of establishing the initial relationship between the two – a necessity for the balance of the film to work.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: Chloe Domont has tight and firm control over her sharply scripted Fair Play, a gripping debut exploring power, gender, and sexual dynamics with outstandingly complex and explosive lead performances from Phoebe Dynevor and Alden Ehrenreich
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: Chloe Domont creates a stellar debut with her meticulous filmmaking and nostalgic demonstration of tension, matched with powerful performances by her leads Phoebe Dynevor and Alden Ehrenreich.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: What makes Fair Play so fascinating is the modern ideas put into the mindset of the thrillers we used to see regularly in the ’90s, not a perfect example of the genre but an exploration of a style of movies that have been missing for quite some time.
reviews.author: Rachel Leishman

reviews.text: It’s a gripping character and relationship study that gives its stars heavy material to bring to life in a thrilling film worth its salt
reviews.author: Gissane Sophia

reviews.text: It all feels like a handful of David Mamet scripts reduced down in a pot with much of the misanthropy and all the tartly memorable dialogue skimmed off the top.
reviews.author: Andrew Dignan

reviews.text: It’s an incisive study of workplace power dynamics. It’s a critique of the testosterone palaces that uphold the banking industry. It’s an investigation into a corrosive, self-worth-burning romance.
reviews.author: Yasmin Omar

reviews.text: Fair Play is a polarizing thriller that’s truly visceral, leaving the viewer uncomfortable and demands a critical analysis without easy answers or even simple truths
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: More an introduction to the erotic-thriller genre than an immediate classic, Fair Play is a slickly made tale of twisted love that keeps you holding your breath until the end.
reviews.author: Sophie Butcher

reviews.text: Steamy and sexy as hell, as jagged as shards of broken glass…and as pointed as the tip of a stiletto heel.
reviews.author: Neil Pond

reviews.text: FAIR PLAY may not be as smart & original as it initially seems, but the momentum, central performances, & cranked-up drama are engaging. Although [it] neglects its more original start, the film [is] an engrossing takedown of fragile male entitlement...
reviews.author: Jim Ross

reviews.text: The screenplay by writer/director Chloe Domont combines suspense, romance, drama and thrills with mixed results.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: Chloe Domont’s directorial debut is a slick navigation through the psychological warfare to  play the game of corporate America.
reviews.author: Jillian Chilingerian

reviews.text: This sizzling psychological thriller is a lot more fun than it probably should be. Because premiering writer/director Chole Domont is tackling some heavy duty stuff here.
reviews.author: Joanna Langfield

reviews.text: It goes too far, too often, and becomes uncomfortable and triggering to watch.
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: Power shifts, suspenseful backstabbing, massive amounts of alcohol consumption, the breaking down of a sexual relationship, and bucking traditional structures all play a hand in this film's poker game.
reviews.author: Matthew Creith

reviews.text: a relationship thriller with loads of dramatic tension...Unfortunately, once the inevitable happens, Domont takes things so over the top, and multiple times at that, that any impact her film had gets lost in the ludicrousness of her final act.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: [Domont's] thrilling mastery of slow-burn tension, insightful examination of power dynamics in business and personal relationships, and creation of exceptional performances prove Domont to be a director with a singular voice.
reviews.author: Marya E. Gates

reviews.text: Domont nearly puts together the debut of the year, it still shows incredible promise. There are plenty of highlight sequences in Fair Play to show she’s barely scratched the surface of her potential.
reviews.author: Alan French

reviews.text: A thriller that not only gets provocation right but drapes it in barbed wire, slicing through the false declarations and reassurances that mitigate the true role gender politics continue to play in each relationship and environment.
reviews.author: Prabhjot Bains

reviews.text: Fair Play is the captivating psychological thriller that will have your heart flying right out of your chest. Chloe Dormont direction/writing is UNFORGETTABLE, Phoebe Dynevor & Alden Ehrenreich are INTENSE.
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text: With astuteness and clarity, Domont takes Fair Play to unexpected places, refusing to halt to give us a breather. The pacing is so incredible that it mimics the emotional claustrophobia of a chamber drama.
reviews.author: Ishita Sengupta

reviews.text: Fair Play is a harrowing drama that features one mesmerizing scene after another.
reviews.author: Brian Rowe

reviews.text: Fair Play is a taut two hander featuring Phoebe Dynevor and Alden Ehrenreich on scenery chewing form, and benefits from an understated Eddie Marsan as trading supremo Campbell.
reviews.author: Martin Carr

reviews.text: Equating emasculation with empowerment, this incredibly problematic film sends a dangerous message that women can’t be powerful unless men aren’t. It’s dated and sexist rather than smart and provocative.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: What’s perhaps most miraculous about this tight and taut film is Domont’s unforgiving economy. There isn’t a single expendable moment in Domont’s gradually escalating, fiery ride
reviews.author: Tomris Laffly

reviews.text: To describe Chloe Domont’s Fair Play as an “erotic thriller” is to misinterpret the genre. It’s also doing a disservice to the fantastic way the director depicts the calculated insanity of her characters.
reviews.author: Soham Gadre

reviews.text: The film feels dangerous at times, volatile, and isn’t afraid to get ugly when it needs to. I absolutely can’t wait to see how the world responds to this one (I suspect it will be divisive) and what filmmaker Domont has in store for us next.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: Examining the evils of corporate culture has been done before (The Wolf of Wall Street). But this time, a twisted feminist perspective adds fresh verve.
reviews.author: Dwight Brown

reviews.text: Fair Play is an intense, gripping thriller from Chloe Domont. The interplay between Dynevor and Ehrenreich is sharp, the tension rises to a full boil and the politics (both office and sexual) are driven to breaking point. A true winner.
reviews.author: Harris Dang

reviews.text: Phoebe Dynevor's intense performance gives the film its groove.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: Critics are hailing 'Fair Play' as the return of the erotic thriller and I feel like I’m being gaslit. First of all, its not a thriller.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: It builds tension very well and I was genuinely unsure with what was going to happen and how it would end.
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: Domont’s shrewdly written script keeps us glued to the screen and her keen direction shows an incredible ability to steadily ratchet up the tension. It’s only in the final act that the film stumbles and gets carried away in bringing everything to a close.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: A film star is born and another reinvented in debut director Chloe Domont’s sleek drama of a glamorous couple succumbing to backstabbing and brutal belittling.
reviews.author: Kent Turner

reviews.text: It’s the rare film that manages to substantially comment on one of the most prevailing issues of our current moment (toxic masculinity) while somehow feeling like a throwback adult drama from the ’90s intended for a mass audience.
reviews.author: Daniel Joyaux

reviews.text: Domont's film is about as pitiless as many of its characters, putting toxic masculinity under an unflinching microscope.
reviews.author: Piers Marchant

reviews.text: A good thriller will ramp up the anxiety with each step as it hurtles towards its conclusion, and Fair Play does not let up until the very end, offering a twisted and toxic tale of a couple driven to the brink by a shift in power dynamics.
reviews.author: Therese Lacson

reviews.text: The onus is on the men, and the men alone, to behave better. And that's exactly how it should be.
reviews.author: Emma Baty

reviews.text: Has the distinction of being both slick and thorny at the same time — and utterly arresting.
reviews.author: Candice Frederick

reviews.text: Writer-director Chloe Domont crafts a sharp and tense psychological thriller that examines gender office politics with brutal honesty.
reviews.author: Sara Clements

reviews.text: A searing study of masculine insecurity in a vicious world of soul-crushing sharks, it features a stunning performance from Phoebe Dynevor, well matched with Alden Ehrenreich, doing his best film work in years, maybe ever.
reviews.author: Brian Tallerico

reviews.text: Both leads do formidable work, and Domont does a wicked job of ratcheting up the tension. Two memorable scenes are instant classics: The opening sex scene with a surprise twist, and an engagement party argument where true natures are revealed.
reviews.author: Frank J. Avella

reviews.text: Fair Play is caustic and enthralling, but mostly it’s the kind of movie that makes you wince with recognition... if you’ve ever made yourself small to avoid the rage of an insecure man.
reviews.author: Alissa Wilkinson

reviews.text: A fantastic debut, one that explores every day things in a truly unique way.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: A sexy, intelligent thriller for an adult audience.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: The stress this movie put me through is criminal, but that’s mostly due to the intensity of the performances by Dynevor and Ehrenreich.
reviews.author: Valerie Complex

reviews.text: An explosive, fast-paced relationship drama/thriller that casts an unflinching look at feminism on Wall Street.
reviews.author: Lauren Coates

reviews.text: Only so much one person can take in the face of elevated jealousy. If one woman can disrupt a whole ecosystem, 'Fair Play' adequately asked how functional that assembly can be.
reviews.author: Murjani Rawls

reviews.text: A razor-sharp psychological thriller that dissects sexual politics in the workplace, wealth, corporate greed, and betrayal.
reviews.author: David Gonzalez

reviews.text: Chloe Domont's erotic financial drama is an instant classic.
reviews.author: Santanu Das

reviews.text: “Fair Play” has a glitch in the formula not even the dullest analyst can overlook. It’s a pity when something so smart ends up as something so dumb.
reviews.author: Sarah Manvel

reviews.text: It feels profoundly sad, that in our thirst for coherent adult dramas that mix real-world dynamics with sexual interplay that we are calling something as detached as the tedious interpersonal mechanics of “Fair Play” an erotic thriller.
reviews.author: Andrew Kendall

reviews.text: I'm convinced, I've seen enough, it's time to step back and hand over the keys to Hollywood to Chloe Domont. It's her world now, I am just another analyst who wants to help her succeed.
reviews.author: Alex Billington

reviews.text: The film is, overall, an interesting, dramatically heightened case study in what can go wrong when toxic masculinity rears its ugly head.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: Fair Play has high stakes, bruised egos, and asks some tough questions.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: Using the intensely charged world of high-stakes finance as a backdrop, Fair Play is a surprisingly thrilling relationship drama that tackles gender dynamics in a refreshing way.
reviews.author: Wilson Kwong

reviews.text: Phoebe Dynevor and Alden Ehrenreich are brilliant as lovers and co-workers willing to slash Cupid’s throat for career advancement.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: The worthiness of its subject matter alone is not enough to save this buttoned-up psychodrama from fizzling out before it really catches fire.
reviews.author: Hannah Strong

reviews.text: It is highly impressive that this is Domont’s directorial debut. She not only brings out the best in her actors but also knows how to accentuate the themes of her screenplay through some taut direction.
reviews.author: Giovanni Lago

reviews.text: A twisty relationship drama about the secretive thrill of a workplace affair that morphs into a psychological thriller about the insecurity of having to report to your partner. Reimagines the workplace as a gladiatorial arena, the work as a bloodsport.
reviews.author: Gayle Sequeira

reviews.text: Modern relationships between man, woman, and work are explored in this provocative and often uncomfortable thriller. Domont immediately asserts herself as a talent to watch, complemented perfectly by two storming lead performances.
reviews.author: Kat Hughes

reviews.text: "Fair Play is an explosive and audacious debut that earns every second of its tautly wound twist and turns. Domont, who also wrote the film, is clearly a talent to be reckoned with, and Fair Play hints at the exceptional promise to come."
reviews.author: Cate Young

reviews.text: This is a slickly shot piece that has strong tension throughout, and its biting examination of power & gender dynamics in the workplace and relationships sheds a bright light on the kind of abusive behavior that making large sums of money tends to excuse.
reviews.author: Aaron White

reviews.text: Dynevor is a stellar actress, and she finds gradations of rage and desire that poor Ehrenreich can’t begin to achieve. In “Fair Play,” it’s an unfair comparison between them.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: A brutal morality tale, depicting the harsh realities of gender dynamics and the corrupting influence of power.
reviews.author: Michael Levine

reviews.text: A thriller about ego, ambition, and impossible love. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Iván Morales

reviews.text: The chemistry between Dynevor and Ehrenreich is unpredictably suspenseful, supported by a sizzling script of scorching arguments and punchy dialogue that Domont refuses to snuff.
reviews.author: Emily Maskell

reviews.text: Domont’s multi-layered understanding of genre tropes, i.e., when to use, tweak, or otherwise subvert conventions typically associated with finance dramas and romantic thrillers, keeps Fair Play from becoming stale or tiresome.
reviews.author: Mel Valentin

reviews.text: Not only showcasing a masterful effort of filmmaking by Chloe Domont, but also a powerhouse duo of wickedness in Phoebe Dynevor and Alden Ehrenreich, Fair Play is a breakout hit of the festival!
reviews.author: Carson Timar

reviews.text: Quibbles aside, it’s good to see a genre movie tackling gender conflict in rigorously nondidactic ways, making this an auspicious debut for Domont.
reviews.author: David Rooney

reviews.text: The plotting is meticulous, with a tricky financial subplot and a looming engagement party that build towards a truly crushing climax.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: [A] prickly thriller about a couple whose efforts to stay together are complicated by their ambitious industry, workplace, and hearts.
reviews.author: Nick Schager

reviews.text: They don't make thrillers like this anymore. Chloe Domont delivers the type of feature debut you could only wish for. It's sexy, gripping, and at times terrifying.
reviews.author: EJ Moreno

reviews.text: Domont’s directorial debut has a coherent narrative and earns our good graces with its technical craftsmanship and assured performances. Yet it doesn’t forge new ground exploring the tired, sexist notion that men are threatened by successful women
reviews.author: Courtney Howard

reviews.text: As confident as writer-director Chloe Domont is with high-finance gamesmanship, she’s sharper as a dramatist of premarital decay among millennials.
reviews.author: Chuck Bowen

reviews.text: ... Despite a somewhat underdeveloped third act, the movie eventually finds its way to a satisfying conclusion that managed to make me cheer for Wall Street corruption.
reviews.author: Anna Menta

reviews.text: Chloe Domont’s crackling psychological drama coupled with palpable performances by Phoebe Dynevor and Alden Ehrenreich unsparingly challenges personal and professional power dynamics.
reviews.author: Eric Marchen

reviews.text: There certainly are enough layers to Fair Play for many interpretations, but here's one. Emily's promotion exposes Luke's toxic masculinity, which seals his fate.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: Fair Play balances the needs of a proper corporate nail-biter and a piece of filthy, sweaty, Michelin-starred trash.
reviews.author: David Fear

reviews.text: A complete triumph - the biggest and best debut of Sundance 2023 so far. With two pitch perfect performances this is an intense thriller that will make your heart race, and your blood rush.
reviews.author: Nathan McVay

reviews.text: A no-nonsense story that takes a scalpel to harsh work environments and the character’s toxic need for control, Fair Play reaches its final destination with grit and grime.
reviews.author: Allyson Johnson

reviews.text: Fair Play is a corporate barn burner and relationship psychosexual drama that’s thrilling as it is brutally precise in its study of power, sex, attraction, and ambition.
reviews.author: Karl Delossantos

reviews.text: Chloe Domont’s compellingly drawn portrait of entitlement, impotence and the amplified conservative values of the bros casting the bones of capitalism is a violent delight
reviews.author: Jacob Oller

reviews.text: Fair Play is a savage, wince-inducing takedown of fragile masculinity and toxic workplaces, abetted by excellent performances from Phoebe Dynevor and Alden Ehrenreich.
reviews.author: Shaun Munro

reviews.text: Fair Play is a ferocious dramatic thriller with bite.
reviews.author: Jeff Nelson

reviews.text: Fair Play is intoxicating and thrilling, unraveling slowly but surely until it reaches a sensational finale that is as crushing as it is powerful.
reviews.author: Mae Abdulbaki

reviews.text: A dynamic corporate thriller that's a lot like the kind of adult dramas we used to get in the nineties.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: “Fair Play” is complex enough, and anchored by excellent performances from Dynevor (strong and believable) and Ehrenreich (toxic, vulnerable and very different from Han Solo), so as not to disappoint. Fascinating. Full review in Spanish,
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: Nearly every line of dialogue thrown between Emily and Luke is ripe with an undertone of sinister intentions or subtext reading. It’s all thanks to Domont’s subtle direction and dynamite performances from Dynevor and Ehrenreich.
reviews.author: Kevin L. Lee

reviews.text: Chloe Domont’s script and tight direction turn this into a sharp and incisive thriller.
reviews.author: Karen M. Peterson

reviews.text: A Couple Experiences Shifting Power Dynamics In This High-Stakes Thriller.
reviews.author: Ben Pearson

reviews.text: A wicked-sharp psychological thriller that marks the scarily assured feature debut of the writer-director Chloe Domont.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: It’s a grim, dynamic thriller, one that sets workplace and home crashing into one another in a small symphony of beautiful disharmony.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: “Fair Play,” while full of sex, money, corporate backstabbing, and a lot of other things that are fun to watch, really is a good little movie.
reviews.author: Owen Gleiberman

reviews.text: [A] steamy, razor-wired, barking-mad movie...
reviews.author: Ryan Lattanzio

reviews.text: Domont cooly constructs a contemporary story about how a gendered disparity in finance and power can wreck a seemingly successful relationship.
reviews.author: Benjamin Lee

reviews.text: Domont crafts a complicated, but wildly entertaining knockout of a film exploring how fragile a relationship built on money and power can be.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: 'Fair Play' is frustratingly reactionary in its sexual politics – and not quite willing to either subvert or grapple with that in a genuinely thought-provoking way.
reviews.author: Jason Bailey

reviews.text: Chloe Domont’s feature debut Fair Play cuts deep even as it comes dangerously close to careening off the cliff of plausibility with a screenplay that dips into sophomoric.
reviews.author: Jordan Raup

synopsis: When a coveted promotion at a cutthroat financial firm arises, once supportive exchanges between lovers Emily (Phoebe Dynevor) and Luke (Alden Ehrenreich) begin to sour into something more sinister. As the power dynamics irrevocably shift in their relationship, the couple must face the true price of success and the unnerving limits of ambition. In her feature debut, writer-director Chloe Domont weaves a taut relationship thriller, staring down the destructive gender dynamics that pit partners against each other in a world that is transforming faster than the rules can keep up. Also starring Eddie Marsan, Rich Sommer, and Sebastian De Souza, Fair Play unravels the uncomfortable collision of empowerment and ego.
